newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs, pork bellies tumble to sharply lower end.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs, pork bellies tumble to sharply lower end.

text.p: A combination of weak fundamental factors and technical pressure pushed CME lean hog and pork belly futures down for sharp losses again Monday.
Hogs closed 1.175 to 0.225 cent per lb lower with October off most at 69.850 cents. Pork bellies ended off 1.200 to 2.250 with February off 1.675 at 69.950 cents.

October hogs slipped to 69.575 cents, the lowest level since March 26, before values recovered somewhat. There was chart support at that level but the market remained pressured by weak cash hog indications for Tuesday and slow pork sales to domestic and foreign buyers , traders said.
"The cash (hog market) continues to be weaker and the demand situation (for pork) remains lackluster," said Karl Skold, director of research for Frontier Risk Management.

Traders and analysts alike cited lighter-than-expected demand from Japan which is coming during a slow domestic usage period. Japanese trade house buyers said pork imports were up in July, but not necessarily from the U.S. Pork prices in the U.S. were too high compared with European pork, they added.
Also, the European Union also reported hog numbers were up in the spring there despite Dutch reductions due to swine fever.
